author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read SQL Server Audit events (event 33205) from the Windows Application or Security log. NXLog or the Snare agent forwards them in Snare format over syslog to the data collector, the feed of the Sophos Windows Event Log integration. Logins and logouts go to Auth and every other action goes to ManagementEvent.
notes:
Setup:
- SQL Server Audit is written to the Windows Application or Security log (event 33205) and forwarded in Snare format over syslog by NXLog or the Snare agent, the feed of the Sophos Windows Event Log integration.
- Create a server audit TO APPLICATION_LOG or TO SECURITY_LOG and add the action groups you want, such as SUCCESSFUL_LOGIN_GROUP, FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP, SERVER_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP and SCHEMA_OBJECT_ACCESS_GROUP.
- Each parser is a child of the global parser SNARE_Unsupported, which takes Snare events no other built-in parser handles.
- As a child of Microsoft_Windows_SNARE_Master each parser would compete with SNARE_Unsupported (see the Sysmon entry).

Saving in the console:
- To add each in Sophos Fusion, choose Add Custom Parser, tick Set Global Parent in Parser Script and keep Parent parser (default): the parent picker lists only your own parsers, never built-in ones.
- Paste the whole file, !PARENT line included; its !SCHEMA line sets the schema, whatever the dialog shows.
- Without that option the save fails with "code contains restricted syntax: !PARENT"; turn the option on in the editor and save again.
- Saved this way in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15, each parser gave the same Run Test results while still disabled.

Field mapping:
- Logins and logouts (LGIS, LGIF, LGO, and DBAS, DBAF and DBL for contained database users) go to Auth, with the login as target user, the client address and workstation, the instance as service, and for failed logins the 18456 state mapped to a failure category.
- Every other action goes to ManagementEvent: the action code as operation and its name as operation_name, the statement as a T-SQL query, the login, client, database and result.
- Fields are read by name, so the layouts of SQL Server 2016 to 2025 all parse.

Time:
- The event time is event_time, which SQL Server writes in UTC.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the field order of SQL Server's event log text and the Snare and NXLog output formats.

Testing:
- Each parser passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15, taking all of its lines in each of 15 Run Tests (169 of 169 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs).
- In Run Test the Snare parent also sets target_host, and os on ManagementEvent lines, fields the engine stores but the docs' schema tables don't list.

Known gaps:
- A statement over 4,000 characters arrives in several records.
